text:
A: Hiya! Oh, it's you, I spotted your dog lead in your picture! I'm Gemma.
B: Ha, Nicola! That's Biscuit's lead. She's in her bed just down there, you'll probably hear her snoring in a minute.
A: Aw, we've got a snorer too, Duke, he's my mum and dad's Staffie. He's ancient. What's Biscuit?
B: Jack Russell, and she's getting on as well, twelve now. Proper stubborn. She won't go out if it's raining, just plants her feet on the doorstep.
A: Oh my God, I see that every week at work! I'm a dog groomer, well, assistant, and we've got this cockapoo who absolutely hates the dryer. She sort of tries to climb up you, do you know what I mean?
B: Ah no, bless her. A groomer, that's lovely. Do you get bitten much?
A: Erm, not loads. You learn to read them. With the nervous ones you just go slow and talk to them, and most of them settle. It's the owners that are harder sometimes, when you've got to tell them the dog's matted to the skin and they don't want to hear it.
B: That's my job exactly! I'm a dental hygienist. You've got to tell people their gums are bleeding without making them feel told off. Same thing really, isn't it? Just with less fur.
A: Ha! Less fur. Yeah. Do you like it?
B: I do, honestly. It's two days a week. I went part-time after my divorce so I could be around for the kids. Have you got kids? I thought you looked like a busy mum in your photo, sorry if that's wrong!
A: No, no kids! That's my nieces in the picture. I'm a professional auntie. Erm, all my friends have got kids though, so I sort of get the busy mum bit second-hand.
B: Being an auntie's the best bit anyway, you get to hand them back.
A: That's what my mum says! How old are yours?
B: Megan's twenty, she's at uni in Cardiff, and Alfie's fifteen. He's got his GCSEs next year so I'm trying not to nag. Failing, but trying.
A: Is it weird with your daughter away?
B: Erm, yeah, a bit. More than I let on, probably. The house is quieter. She rings when she wants money, ha.
A: I'm doing a degree as well, actually, Open University, psychology. So I'm sort of a student too, just thirty-five and living with my mum and dad.
B: Oh, good for you! Psychology, what do you want to do with it?
A: Something in mental health, maybe counselling. I had counselling myself in my twenties and it really helped, so. Sorry, that's a bit heavy for three minutes, isn't it?
B: No, not at all, that's a proper good reason to do it. You'd be brilliant, you're easy to talk to.
A: Aw, thank you. What do you do for fun then?
B: Gigs, mostly. There's a venue in Frome, the Cheese and Grain, and I'm going to a tribute night there in a couple of weeks. And swimming, and netball, the back-to-netball thing.
A: I do Zumba! Wednesdays. It nearly killed me last week.
B: Ha, I've seen those classes, they're no joke. Do you go with friends?
A: Yeah, with my mate Kirsty. We mostly go so we can have a Greggs after and not feel guilty.
B: That's the only reason to exercise, honestly. Did you do that puzzle at the start, by the way? I was hopeless.
A: Me too! The bloke I just had said two of them had more than one right answer, so I'm blaming the puzzle.
B: Ooh, I like that, we'll blame the—
